Question B-006-012-007.

Why the correct answer is right: Traps can make an antenna resonant on more than one frequency, including frequencies related to transmitter harmonics, so a trapped antenna may radiate harmonics more readily if they are present.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "It is too sharply directional at lower frequencies": Traps affect electrical length and multiband resonance. They do not make the antenna excessively directional at the lower frequencies.
- sourceIndex 2: "It picks up more noise than a simple dipole": A trap does not inherently make the antenna a better noise pickup device. The noted disadvantage is possible harmonic radiation.
- sourceIndex 3: "It can only be used for one band": That is the opposite of why traps are installed. Trap antennas are commonly used to cover more than one band.
